'''''Baldellia ranunculoides''''', the '''lesser water-plantain''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Alismataceae]].

==Synonyms==
Alisma ranunculoides, Echinodorus ranunculoides, Sagittaria ranunculodes

==Description==
''Baldellia ranunculoides'' is an [[aquatic plant]] which produced erect flowering stems that rise up to {{convert|10|cm|0}} above the water surface.<ref name="Farmer">{{cite web |url=http://www.plant-identification.co.uk/skye/alismataceae/baldellia-ranunculoides.htm |work=West Highland Flora |title=Lesser water-plantain, ''Baldellia ranunculoides'' |author=Carl Farmer |year=2003 |access-date=December 1, 2013 |archive-date=June 2, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130602063335/http://www.plant-identification.co.uk/skye/alismataceae/baldellia-ranunculoides.htm }}</ref> Each flower stalk bears one or two [[umbel]]s of up to five [[flower]]s each, and often only a single flower. Each flower is {{convert|10|-|15|mm|1}} in diameter, and has three petals.<ref name="Farmer"/> When not in flower, ''B. ranunculoides'' can be mistaken for lesser spearwort, ''[[Ranunculus flammula]]'', which grows in similar locations.<ref name="Farmer"/>

==Distribution==
''Baldellia ranunculoides'' is found along the Atlantic and Baltic coast of western and northern [[Europe]], and along the [[Mediterranean]] coasts of southern [[Europe]], [[Turkey]] and [[North Africa]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.arkive.org/lesser-water-plantain/baldellia-ranunculoides/ |title=Lesser water-plantain (''Baldellia ranunculoides'') |publisher=[[ARKive]] |access-date=December 1, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131204030338/http://www.arkive.org/lesser-water-plantain/baldellia-ranunculoides/ |archive-date=2013-12-04 }}</ref><ref>[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=300116 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/index1.php?scientific-name=baldellia+ranunculoides|title=Baldellia ranunculoides [Mestolaccia minore]|website=luirig.altervista.org|language=it|access-date=2017-01-26}}</ref>  Recently found in eastern Newfoundland, Bristol's Hope barachois, Avalon Peninsula, the only location in North America. May have been introduced by a float (Sarracenia magazine, Newfoundland and Labrador Wildflower Society.
